description.value: The study investigated neural activation associated with cognitive reappraisal of sadness in healthy school-age children using fMRI, including whole-brain, amygdala subregion ROI, and meta-analysis-derived ROI analyses.

spans.text: The objectives of the current study were to investigate the neural correlates of cognitive reappraisal of sadness in sample of healthy school-age children.

description.value: Nineteen healthy children aged 8–12 years participated in an fMRI study with repeated-measures cognitive reappraisal conditions and five task runs.

value: Ten out of 23 regions showed a significant effect of passive viewing versus reappraising sad stimuli at p < .05, and an additional four regions showed trend-level effects at p < .10. The pattern of activation in all significant or trend-level regions was in the same direction as reported in the Diekhof meta-analysis. The strongest effects were in dorsomedial PFC, left middle and inferior frontal cortex, and left anterior insula.

stimuli.value: Neutral and sad photographs from the International Affective Picture Series and an in-house set of child-appropriate images.

spans.text: Stimuli were taken from the International Affective Picture Series ( Bradley et al., 2001 ,  Bradley et al., 2008 ) and were supplemented for from an in-house set of images selected to be appropriate for viewing by children (e.g., photos of other children crying).
Responses were made on a 4-button box.
Children had 4 s to rate their negative affect, on a scale from 1 to 4.

instructions.value: Children were instructed to passively view neutral and sad photos and to actively decrease their experience of negative emotions in response to sad images using positive cognitive reappraisal strategies. VIEW indicated non-regulation trials, MAKE-POSITIVE indicated regulation trials, and children rated how they felt on a 1–4 negative-affect scale.

spans.text: Children were instructed to decrease their experience of negative emotions in response to viewing sad images using positive cognitive reappraisal strategies.
Children's self-reported use of cognitive reappraisal ER strategies was assessed using the 4-item positive refocusing subscale of CERQ-k ( Garnefski et al., 2007 ).

description.value: A four-item positive refocusing subscale assessing children's self-reported attempts to reframe negative events positively.

spans.text: This is a well-validated subscale (alpha = .80 in our sample) that assess the degree to which children report trying to reframe their experience of negative events in a more positive light.
